title: Bi-qutrit entangled edge states of positive partial transposes with largest ranks
abstract: Whenever $E$ is an eight dimensional subspace of the bi-qutrit quantum system whose orthogonal complement is spanned by a vector of Schmidt rank three, we show that there exist PPT entangled edge states with the range space $E$ whose partial transposes are of rank six, which is the largest possible rank. In this way, we exhibit a huge family of bi-qutrit PPT entangled edge states of type $(8,6)$. They make faces of the convex set of all PPT states, and we find bi-qutrit PPT entangled edge states of other types on the boundaries of such faces.
summary: The paper mathematically characterizes bi-qutrit entangled edge states that satisfy the Positive Partial Transpose (PPT) criterion. By analyzing the geometry of the set of all PPT states, the authors construct specific families of high-rank states and map out their existence on the boundaries of key faces within this state space.
main_problem: The primary goal is characterizing the structure of the convex set $P$ of all Positive Partial Transpose (PPT) quantum states, specifically focusing on identifying PPT entangled edge states.
main_result: The authors exhibit a large family of bi-qutrit PPT entangled edge states of type $(8,6)$ and demonstrate how other types can be found on the boundaries of the faces defining this set.
method: The analysis involves rigorous mathematical characterization using concepts like faces of convex sets, analyzing rank conditions for partial transposes, and solving systems of linear equations derived from positivity constraints.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum states ($\varrho$) within the bi-qutrit system ($3 \otimes 3$). The mathematical framework involves defining these states relative to subspaces $E$ and analyzing their partial transposes $\varrho^\Gamma$.
key_observables: Ranks of the state ($	ext{rank}(\varrho)$) and its partial transpose ($	ext{rank}(\varrho^\Gamma)$); the classification type $(p_h, k_q)$.
important_parameters: The dimensions (bi-qutrit system), specific parameters defining the states ($a_i, b_i, r, \alpha_i$), and the Schmidt rank of associated kernel vectors.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes the existence of a kernel vector $|\zetaangle$ with a specified Schmidt rank (e.g., three) to cover generic cases in $\mathbb{C}^3 \otimes \mathbb{C}^3$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates lower and upper bounds on the ranks for $3\otimes 3$ PPT entangled edge states. Figure 2 uses geometric arguments involving intersecting circles/discs to prove the existence of suitable parameters.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the mathematical constraints (PPT condition, face structure) for the bi-qutrit system. It then constructs specific families of states achieving high ranks (e.g., type $(8,6)$) and explores related boundary cases by varying parameters within the defined faces.
why_interesting: This work provides deep structural insights into entanglement detection in small quantum systems using necessary conditions like PPT, which is fundamental for understanding resource theories in quantum information.
